root_cause.text: In the i915 DRM atomic plane handling, `unlink_nv12_plane()` was invoked after `plane_atomic_check()` had already populated the new `intel_plane_state`, so when a plane stopped being an NV12 Y plane the unlink code could overwrite/clobber valid state fields in `intel_plane_state` due to the incorrect call order and removed visibility guard.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE says “`plane_atomic_check()` will first compute the proper plane state based on the userspace request, and `unlink_nv12_plane()` later clears some of the state,” and the patch moves `unlink_nv12_plane()` to run earlier in `intel_plane_set_invisible()` and changes `icl_check_nv12_planes()` to call it unconditionally before state computation; it also notes the bug was introduced when the “visible check” was removed in `unlink_nv12_plane()` (`Fixes: 6a01df2f1b2a`).

intent_record.intent_summary: Ensure invisible planes are unlinked from NV12 state before their active flags are cleared.
intent_record.what: A forward declaration for static function `unlink_nv12_plane(struct intel_crtc_state *crtc_state, struct intel_plane_state *plane_state)` was added, and `intel_plane_set_invisible()` now calls `unlink_nv12_plane(crtc_state, plane_state)` before clearing the plane's bits from `active_planes`, `scaled_planes`, and `nv12_planes`.
intent_record.how: When a plane is made invisible, any NV12-specific linkage is now removed first, ensuring related NV12 state is detached before the plane is marked inactive. This prevents stale NV12 plane associations from persisting in the CRTC state.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a guard in NV12 plane unlinking to skip processing when no linked plane is present.
intent_record.what: In `unlink_nv12_plane()`, a new early return was added: if `plane_state->planar_linked_plane` is NULL, the function now exits immediately before clearing the field or performing any further unlink logic.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now avoids attempting to unlink an NV12 plane when no linked planar partner exists, preventing redundant work and avoiding invalid dereference or inconsistent state updates during plane teardown.

intent_record.intent_summary: Always unlink matching NV12 planes during validation to fix cases where linked-plane cleanup was being skipped.
intent_record.what: The conditional check `if (plane_state->planar_linked_plane)` before calling `unlink_nv12_plane(crtc_state, plane_state);` was removed, so `unlink_nv12_plane()` is now called unconditionally for every matching plane state in the loop.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the code will attempt to unlink NV12 plane state regardless of whether `planar_linked_plane` is set, which broadens the cleanup path and ensures any relevant plane is detached instead of being skipped due to that flag.

This group only adds a null/absence guard for unlinking when no linked plane exists, which does not address the state overwrite caused by the call order.

candidates.rationale: This pre-fix visibility check could skip unlinking an NV12-linked plane when the plane state had already been populated, allowing stale linked-plane state to remain and later be clobbered by incorrect cleanup ordering.

Clearing the NV12 plane bit here is part of the state cleanup path; if unlink_nv12_plane() runs after plane_atomic_check() has populated new state, this kind of cleanup can overwrite valid intel_plane_state fields associated with the plane.

vuln_statements.explanation: This visibility guard could prevent unlinking an NV12-linked plane once plane_atomic_check() had already populated the new intel_plane_state, leaving stale linked-plane state in place and enabling the later cleanup ordering bug to clobber valid fields.

This matches the vulnerable construct described: `unlink_nv12_plane()` is able to clobber already-populated state when a plane stops being NV12/Y-plane-related, because it clears visibility/state after the atomic check has populated `intel_plane_state`.
